details.description: No parameter defaults, return value details, or error semantics are documented.
details.why_required: Callers must know defaults (`retries`, `delayMs`), what is returned (`string`), and what errors to expect so they can write correct handling logic.
details.code_evidence: Defaults in source: `const retries = options?.retries ?? 3;` and `const delayMs = options?.delayMs ?? 1000;`. Return is `res.text()` and errors include `throw new Error("Request failed")` and re-throw of caught errors.

details.description: Behavior and valid ranges for `RetryOptions` are not described (e.g. effect of `retries: 0`, acceptable `delayMs`).
details.why_required: Incorrect option values may produce surprising behavior (the code contains an
throw if the retry loop is skipped).
details.code_evidence: `while (attempt < retries) { ... }` and final `throw new Error("Unreachable");` indicate unexpected behavior when `retries` <= 0.

details.description: No documentation explains which errors are thrown, which are retried, or describes the behavior on non-OK HTTP responses.
details.why_required: Callers need to distinguish retriable from terminal errors and implement correct retry/backoff or reporting logic.
details.code_evidence: On non-OK responses the code `throw new Error("Request failed")` is executed; network rejections are caught and retried.
